statement: Represent a mesh in a half-edge data structure so faces may have any number of sides and adjacency is cheap to query.
superiority: Native half-edge mesh kernel type with n-gon support across the whole application, no separate library.

acceptance.corpus: Cube, n-gon dome of 200 faces, 1M triangle mesh
acceptance.tolerance: Round-trip face-vertex equality exact; adjacency query scales with returned count

statement: Convert between Rhino meshes and half-edge meshes, preserving n-gon structure.
superiority: Lossless n-gon preservation and indices stable across conversion.

acceptance.corpus: Mesh with 100 n-gons and mixed tri/quad
acceptance.tolerance: Face and vertex counts equal; n-gon structure retained 100%

notes: Forum thread discusses preserving Rhino n-gon structure when converting.

statement: Query vertex positions, face centres, face vertices and halfedges around vertices from a half-edge mesh.

source.ref: Plankton vertex, face and halfedge queries

superiority: Batch queries that return typed trees with no scripting.

acceptance.tolerance: Query results equal reference traversal exactly

notes: Forum thread notes GetPositions returning Point3d values and basic topology-extraction components.

statement: Change topology locally with Euler operators such as edge collapse, face split and vertex split without managing raw data structure.

source.ref: Plankton Euler operators (edge collapse, split face, split vertex)

superiority: Operators are undoable, validity checked and guarantee manifoldness.

acceptance.tolerance: Euler characteristic V-E+F preserved after each valid operation; mesh remains valid

notes: README lists edge collapse and face splitting; forum thread names SplitVertex and SplitFace.

statement: Validate that a mesh is manifold and report problem edges, since half-edge meshes cannot represent non-manifold topology.
superiority: Reports and optionally repairs non-manifold edges and vertices with a clear message.

acceptance.corpus: Mesh with T-junction and bowtie vertex
acceptance.tolerance: All injected non-manifold sites reported; false positives 0

notes: Forum thread states Plankton suits manifold meshes.

statement: Apply Conway operators such as dual, ambo, kis, truncate to meshes to generate polyhedral families.
superiority: Full Conway operator set with exact counts.

acceptance.tolerance: Dual of cube is octahedron; V,E,F match published polyhedra counts exactly

notes: README lists Conway operators as a planned addition; included as a feature the half-edge kernel enables.

statement: Subdivide half-edge meshes with standard subdivision schemes such as Catmull-Clark on n-gon meshes.
superiority: Full scheme set with creases and limit evaluation on n-gons.

acceptance.tolerance: Catmull-Clark masks reproduce published weights within 1e-12

notes: README lists subdivision as a planned addition.

statement: Attach custom per-vertex, per-edge and per-face properties to a half-edge mesh for algorithms.
superiority: Typed attribute channels persisted in the file and visible in the UI.

acceptance.corpus: Mesh with vertex colour and scalar field
acceptance.tolerance: Properties round-trip through save and reload exactly

notes: README lists dynamic per-element properties as planned.

statement: Use the half-edge mesh library outside Rhino through a geometry-agnostic variant.
superiority: Same kernel accessible from headless scripting and CLI.

acceptance.corpus: Mesh algorithm run headless on 10 files
acceptance.tolerance: Headless results equal GUI results bit-for-bit on deterministic tasks

statement: Exchange meshes with Turtle and Weaverbird mesh libraries so older definitions keep working.
superiority: Single mesh type with no conversion step and lossless n-gon support.

acceptance.corpus: Weaverbird output fed to Plankton operators
acceptance.tolerance: Face/vertex data equal after round trip

notes: Fetched forum thread describes Turtle/Weaverbird/Plankton custom parameter relationship.
